sources.title: Kansas Historical Society: Kiowa, Early History and the First Divide
sources.note: Original full indexed state history, uncertainty of remote origins, northern Missouri/Yellowstone traditions and later Black Hills migration. Exact prehistoric archaeological origin claims and problematic language-family terminology not adopted.

sources.title: Kansas Historical Society: Kiowa, Southern Alliance with the Comanche
sources.note: Original full indexed account of about 1790 negotiations, Guikate and Comanche alliance, southern regional power. Specific traditions of personal diplomacy attributed as historical account, not invented dialogue.

sources.title: Kiowa Tribe: About Us
sources.note: Original full indexed tribal history, bison, horses, portability and 1901 allotment opening. Overconfident archaeological Kootenay origin, stereotyped military descriptions and exact final-war-month claim not used.

sources.title: Smithsonian National Museum of Natural History: Lights Out, Kiowa tipi models
sources.note: Direct museum visual-description text, Detailed Description: Tipi Model and Photos. Tsakai model 1897-1904 and family-owned designs distinguished from full-size nineteenth-century original.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: Kiowa cradleboard, about 1895
sources.note: Full indexed original catalogue 2/1137, material and baby-carrier function. Oklahoma location only inferred, early collection history unknown, neither presented as certain.

sources.title: James Mooney: Calendar History of the Kiowa Indians, 1898
sources.note: Original Smithsonian PDF full indexed extract, printed page 261, figure 64 and Winter 1833-1834 account. Direct fetch exceeded 48 MB tool limit. Query: site:repository.si.edu "METEORIC SHOWER" "1833". Mooney’s derogatory interpretation of Native beliefs is not adopted.

sources.title: National Archives: Medicine Lodge Creek Treaty and Lone Wolf case
sources.note: Direct 2023 archival presentation of 1867 treaty and 1903 litigation. Avoid precise aggregate acreage and oversimplified legal jurisdiction conclusions; historical court outcome only.

sources.title: Texas Parks and Wildlife: Palo Duro Canyon history
sources.note: Direct Battle of Palo Duro section, September 28, 1874 attack, destruction of supplies and horses, forced return to reservation. Broad claim Native history ended not adopted; no precise horse total.

sources.title: National Museum of the American Indian: The Photography of Horace Poolaw
sources.note: Original full indexed exhibition narrative and named photograph captions, twentieth-century community life. No reproduction of copyrighted photographs.

sources.title: William C. Meadows: More than Meets the Eye, NMAI Magazine, Summer 2025
sources.note: Direct anthropologist’s reported observation at Kiowa community center, marked bone, drumming and score sticks. Local least-sticks rule distinguished from other nations’ variations.

sources.title: Kiowa Tribe: Language Department and bilingual lessons
sources.note: Direct bilingual lesson link text: Hàyá èm bánmà? / Where are you going? Also 2025-2026 teacher training and multiple orthographies. Exact [Gáuigú self-name appears in separate We are Kiowa lesson, supporting alias identity. No video-transcript claim.

sources.title: State Historical Society of North Dakota: Double Ditch Village history
sources.note: Original indexed state site history, earthlodge village, crops, surplus exchange and hunting. No precise household population extrapolated to all Mandan communities.

sources.title: State Historical Society of North Dakota: Introducing Double Ditch
sources.note: Original full indexed educational account: approximately 1490-1785 occupation, four successive ditches and 1780s smallpox/relocation. Approximate archaeological boundaries preserved in prose.

sources.title: Kenneth Kvamme and Stanley Ahler: Integrated Remote Sensing and Excavation at Double Ditch, 2007
sources.note: Primary American Antiquity research abstract, four-year survey, hidden fortifications, hearths and pits verified through excavation. Original 2007 publication distinguished from 2017 online date.

sources.title: MHA community authors, National Park Service: Housing
sources.note: Direct community-authored K-8 Guide to the Earthlodge People excerpt. Mandan clay covering distinguished from Hidatsa sod; women ownership, construction, neighboring relatives and roof socializing. Housing and Subsistence are conservatively combined as one underlying guide for budget checking.

sources.title: MHA community authors, National Park Service: Subsistence, Tribal Nutrition and Health
sources.note: Direct same community-authored K-8 Guide; crop tending, raised drying platforms and lined underground caches. Combined with Housing for conservative source-document budget.

sources.title: National Park Service: Traditional Games, Tchung-kee
sources.note: Original full indexed description, Mandan and Hidatsa game, rolling stone ring and throwing poles. Speculation that expedition members played is not adopted.

sources.title: State Historical Society of North Dakota: Fort Clark history
sources.note: Direct paragraphs on 1830-1831 trading post, 1832 steamboat and 1837 epidemic/survivor relocation. No mortality percentage generalized to all Mandan people.

sources.title: State Historical Society of North Dakota: Sitting Rabbit’s map
sources.note: Direct source, commission in 1905; canvas length 23 feet 4 inches, historical villages and pictorial/oral knowledge. Does not claim completion in 1905 because source also discusses 1906 geography.

sources.title: MHA Nation: History
sources.note: Direct identity and Garrison Dam sections only; separate Mandan, Hidatsa and Arikara identities, dam relocation and fertile bottomland loss. Inconsistent epidemic and artist-visit dates elsewhere on this long page are not adopted.

sources.title: MHA Nation: Mandan welcome
sources.note: Direct homepage explicitly labels the exact phrase Ráátinitak shí’sh. and English translation as Mandan. Modern website text, not a precontact written artifact. Dynamic zero counters ignored.

sources.title: MHA Nation: Culture and Language
sources.note: Direct three distinct language programs, Mandan/Nueta office and mentor/apprentice learning. Modern revitalization, no claim every tribe member speaks all three languages.

sources.title: Edwin Ko, Amanda Foster and Robert Rugh: Mandan ABC Coloring Book, 2016
sources.note: Direct 34-page PDF, publication year 2016 in front matter (PDF index 2), despite 2026 upload directory. Tracing exercises throughout and color-key activity near the end; no inferred visual animal identification.

batchIdentityNotes.decision: Same Kiowa people, separate imported southern territorial polygons. Direct tribal language lesson [Gáuigú bà dàu / We are Kiowa supports self-name. Both dates anachronistic for southern footprint; shared opening explicitly warns and narrative covers north-to-south migration and later polity. Preserve map coverage dates. Composite kiowa-comanche-apache-oklahoma not included; Plains Apache remain a separate people.

Missouri River village-country outline near Bismarck, plausible regional association rather than a precise state border. Mandan-specific narrative distinguishes historic communities, later relocations and contemporary MHA affiliation. Do not absorb composite mandan-hidatsa-and-arikara record: the three living peoples remain distinct.
